c.tagline: The world's longest natural sea beach, ~120 km of Bay of Bengal sand.

taxi.fareNote: Most local trips are by CNG auto-rickshaw, cycle rickshaw, or battery-run tomtom, with fares negotiated before the ride. Uber car coverage is limited, but Pathao (including motorbike rides) is common; confirm fares in the app or with the driver.

emergency.note: 999 is Bangladesh's national emergency line connecting to police, fire, and ambulance.

avoid.reason: Avoid the Rohingya refugee camp areas around Ukhiya and Teknaf (restricted, foreigners need permits) and isolated beach stretches after dark.
Watch for pickpocketing and bag snatching in the crowded main beach and market areas; women may face persistent staring on the beach.

hood_desc: The main and most central beach point, closest to town, with the busiest strip of shops, food stalls, and beach activity; best for first-timers who want to be in the thick of it.
The main hotel-motel zone a little south of Laboni, holding the largest cluster of resorts, restaurants, and easy beach access; a convenient, more upscale base.
A popular beach point between Laboni and Kolatoli known for its seafood-fry stalls and sunset crowds; lively for eating and evening strolls.
A quieter stretch about 30 km south along Marine Drive, with palm-fringed sand and rocky outcrops; scenic and relaxed, home to the big beach resorts.
A hilly area just south of town beside Himchari National Park, where waterfalls and forest meet the sea; a nature and day-trip base rather than a nightlife spot.

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water only; tap water is not potable.

transit.hours: Local buses, CNG auto-rickshaws, and battery-run tomtoms run from around 6:00 AM to 10:00 PM; late-night travel relies on CNG auto-rickshaws and ride-hailing apps.
transit.note: Cox's Bazar has no metro or urban rail; getting around is by CNG auto-rickshaw, cycle rickshaw, battery-run tomtom, and app-based Uber and Pathao, plus a seasonal open-top tourist bus along Marine Drive.
transit.pay: CNG, rickshaw, and tomtom fares are paid in cash and usually negotiated before the ride; there is no transit card system. Ride-hailing apps show fixed fares in the app.

landmarks: Cox's Bazar Beach
Stretching an unbroken 120 kilometres along the Bay of Bengal, the world's longest natural sea beach delivers golden sand, crashing surf and spectacular fiery sunsets.
Inani Beach
South of town, this quieter strand is famed for its coral-strewn shoreline at low tide, emerald hills behind and far fewer crowds than Laboni Point.
Himchari National Park
A forested reserve of hills and waterfalls just down the Marine Drive, crowned by a hilltop viewpoint sweeping over the endless coastline below.
Marine Drive (Cox's Bazar–Teknaf)
An 80-kilometre coastal highway squeezed between green hills and the Bay of Bengal, ranking among Asia's most scenic road trips for beach-hopping travellers.
Aggmeda Khyang
A stilted 19th-century Buddhist monastery of dark timber near the town centre, sheltering bronze Buddha images and manuscripts of the local Rakhine community.
Ramu Buddhist Village
A day-trip village of gilded pagodas and monasteries, including the Bara Khyang and a 100-foot reclining Buddha set among betel groves.
Maheshkhali Island
Reached by speedboat across the bay, this hilly island holds the revered Adinath Temple to Shiva, mangrove fringes and salt-panning villages.
Laboni Beach Point
The town's liveliest beach entrance, buzzing with vendors, beach umbrellas, horse rides and the Burmese Market's souvenir stalls just steps away.
Sonadia Island
A tranquil crescent of dunes, mangroves and fishing hamlets off Maheshkhali, prized by birdwatchers for wintering shorebirds and utterly deserted beaches.
Radiant Fish World
Bangladesh's first large aquarium complex displays sharks, rays and Bay of Bengal species in walk-through tanks, a fun rainy-day stop near the beach.

train.note: The Cox's Bazar railway station (opened December 2023) runs the Cox's Bazar Express and Parjatak Express to Dhaka via Chittagong on the Chittagong–Cox's Bazar line.

bus.note: Long-distance coaches run to Dhaka (~9-12 hours) and Chittagong (~4 hours); AC and non-AC operators leave from the main bus terminal.

intl.to: Saint Martin's Island (Bangladesh) - tourist ships sail from the BIWTA jetty at Nunia Chhara in Cox's Bazar, roughly 5-6 hours each way
intl.op: Karnaphuli Cruise Line and other licensed operators

ferry.note: Since fighting on the Myanmar bank of the Naf River closed the short Teknaf crossing, every ship to Saint Martin's now leaves from Cox's Bazar itself, which makes it a long open-sea day trip rather than a quick hop. The season is short, broadly November to January, and from 2025 the government has capped daily visitor numbers, limited overnight stays and banned tourist visits for much of the year, so confirm the current rules before travelling and book ahead. There are no other scheduled passenger boats from Cox's Bazar - the launches along the beach are excursions, not transport.

half.name: Teknaf
half.blurb: Southernmost town on the Bangladesh mainland, a fishing and border market near the Naf River facing Myanmar.

full.name: Saint Martin's Island
full.blurb: Bangladesh's only coral island, reached by boat from Teknaf, with clear water, coconut groves, and snorkeling over live reef.

full.name: Bandarban Hill District
full.blurb: Hilly Chittagong Hill Tracts town of waterfalls, Buddhist monasteries, and tribal villages reached via winding roads.
